evals.expected_output: No — Prophecy and all other legacy mocking APIs are fully removed in PHPUnit 13; createMock()/createStub() (and the stub/mock builder) are the only test-double API now. The reviewer should flag this as needing a rewrite: e.g. $mock = $this->createMock(PaymentGateway::class); $mock->expects($this->once())->method('charge')->with($this->anything())->willReturn(true); Also worth mentioning sealed doubles (->seal()) as the modern strictness mechanism if the project enables requireSealedMockObjects.
assertions: States explicitly that Prophecy (and other legacy mocking APIs) is fully removed/unsupported in PHPUnit 13, not merely deprecated
States that createMock()/createStub() (and the stub/mock builder methods like getStubBuilder) are the sole test-double API in PHPUnit 13
Provides a rewritten example using $this->createMock() with ->expects()->method()->willReturn() replacing the prophesize()/willReturn() call
Does not claim the prophesize() call will simply keep working under PHPUnit 13
Mentions ->seal() and/or requireSealedMockObjects as the current strictness mechanism for locking a double against unconfigured calls

evals.prompt: Need to wire up code coverage for our src/ directory, generate an HTML report, but exclude src/generated (it's autogenerated DTOs, no point covering that). Also want the report to still show files nobody's test ever touches, not just files with some coverage.
evals.expected_output: Requires an Xdebug or PCOV coverage driver loaded. Configuration via phpunit.xml <source> block with <include><directory suffix=".php">src</directory></include> and <exclude><directory suffix=".php">src/generated</directory></exclude>, plus includeUncoveredFiles="true" (the default) on <source> so zero-coverage files still appear in the report instead of vanishing. Generate the HTML report via phpunit --coverage-html coverage/ (or a <coverage><report><html outputDirectory=...> XML equivalent).
assertions: States that a coverage driver (Xdebug with coverage mode, or PCOV) must be loaded or coverage flags are no-ops
Shows a <source> XML block with <include><directory suffix=".php">src</directory></include> and an <exclude> entry for src/generated
Specifies includeUncoveredFiles="true" and explains it makes zero-coverage files still show up in the report
Shows --coverage-html <dir> (or the <html outputDirectory> XML equivalent) as the command/config to produce the HTML report
Does not claim coverage can be generated with no Xdebug/PCOV driver present

evals.expected_output: Critiques two things: assertEquals on the array is a loose comparison that hides type bugs (e.g. '3' vs 3) and is also order-sensitive here even though order may not matter for a set of IDs — recommend assertSame() if order and type both matter, or one of the order-independent array assertions (assertEqualsCanonicalizing, or assertArraysHaveIdenticalValuesIgnoringOrder) if order genuinely doesn't matter. Also flags assertEquals(3, count($ids)) as reinventing assertCount(3, $ids), which is more specific and produces a better failure diff.
assertions: Flags assertEquals as a loose/type-coercing comparison and recommends a stricter alternative such as assertSame or an order-independent array assertion

Names at least one order-independent array assertion by its actual method name (e.g. assertEqualsCanonicalizing, assertArraysHaveIdenticalValuesIgnoringOrder, or assertArraysAreIdenticalIgnoringOrder)
Flags assertEquals(3, count($ids)) and recommends assertCount(3, $ids) instead
States that more specific assertions produce more useful failure diffs

evals.prompt: Porting some old tests over from a legacy PHPUnit 9 codebase. They're full of stuff like `@dataProvider additionProvider`, `@covers ::add`, `@group slow`, `@depends testEmpty`. What do these become in our PHPUnit 13 setup?
evals.expected_output: PHPUnit 13 uses PHP attributes exclusively for test metadata — docblock @-annotations are not the mechanism at all. @dataProvider -> #[DataProvider('additionProvider')]; @covers -> #[CoversMethod]/#[CoversClass] etc.; @group -> #[Group('slow')]; @depends -> #[Depends('testEmpty')]. Each old docblock annotation should be converted to its native #[...] attribute equivalent, not left as a comment.
assertions: States plainly that PHPUnit 13 uses PHP attributes exclusively and that the old docblock @-annotation syntax is not a supported mechanism
Converts @dataProvider additionProvider to #[DataProvider('additionProvider')]
Converts @group slow to #[Group('slow')]
Converts @depends testEmpty to #[Depends('testEmpty')]
Converts @covers to one of the #[Covers*] attribute family (e.g. #[CoversMethod] or #[CoversClass])
Does not suggest leaving the @-annotations in place as still-functional under PHPUnit 13

evals.prompt: Starting a brand new project, need a phpunit.xml from scratch. We want colors on, a bootstrap file, unit and integration suites, HTML + Clover coverage output for src/, and I want unsealed mocks to count as risky so nobody sneaks in a loose mock.
evals.expected_output: A phpunit.xml with root attributes bootstrap="vendor/autoload.php", colors="true", and requireSealedMockObjects="true" (making an unsealed mock a risky test), a <testsuites> block with unit and integration <testsuite> entries, a <source> block including src with suffix filtering, and a <coverage><report> block listing <html outputDirectory=...> and <clover outputFile=...>.
assertions: Includes requireSealedMockObjects="true" as the root attribute controlling unsealed-mock riskiness
Includes colors="true" and a bootstrap attribute pointing at vendor/autoload.php
Includes a <testsuites> block with separate named <testsuite> entries for unit and integration
Includes a <source><include><directory suffix=".php">src</directory></include></source> block
Includes a <coverage><report> block with both an <html outputDirectory=...> and a <clover outputFile=...> entry
Correctly describes requireSealedMockObjects as flagging unsealed mocks as risky, not as making the build fail outright

evals.prompt: Our CI just started failing because a dependency we call into triggers a deprecation warning deep in its own code — not something we can fix today. I don't want new deprecations from our own code to slip through unnoticed going forward, but I also don't want to be blocked by this one right now. What's the move?
evals.expected_output: Use the baseline workflow: run phpunit --generate-baseline baseline.xml to snapshot today's known issues (including this third-party deprecation), then run with phpunit --use-baseline baseline.xml (or <source baseline="baseline.xml">) so only new issues fail the build going forward. Alternatively/additionally, scope failOnDeprecation more narrowly with failOnIndirectDeprecation left off (or failOnSelfDeprecation/failOnDirectDeprecation turned on) so third-party-triggered noise doesn't block CI while your own deprecated usage still does. Baselines only capture issues seen during test execution, not bootstrap-phase or PHPUnit-internal ones.
assertions: Recommends the baseline workflow: --generate-baseline followed by --use-baseline (or the <source baseline="..."> XML equivalent)
Distinguishes failOnSelfDeprecation / failOnDirectDeprecation / failOnIndirectDeprecation as finer-grained controls by who triggered the deprecation
States that a baseline only captures issues seen during test execution, not bootstrap-phase or PHPUnit-internal issues
Mentions --ignore-baseline as the way to temporarily bypass the baseline if needed
Does not recommend simply suppressing the deprecation with @ or disabling error handling wholesale as the primary fix

evals.prompt: Want our CI pipeline to actually fail the build if any test is risky or throws a PHP warning, not just show green with a warning buried in the output. What flags do I add to the phpunit CLI invocation?
evals.expected_output: Add --fail-on-risky and --fail-on-warning to the CI invocation (e.g. phpunit --fail-on-risky --fail-on-warning), which turn otherwise-non-failing risky/warning outcomes into a non-zero exit code. Notes the XML-attribute equivalents failOnRisky="true" and failOnWarning="true" if they prefer to bake it into phpunit.xml instead, and that other fail-on gates exist too (--fail-on-deprecation, --fail-on-notice, --fail-on-incomplete, --fail-on-skipped).
assertions: Recommends --fail-on-risky specifically for risky tests
Recommends --fail-on-warning specifically for PHP warnings
Mentions the XML-attribute equivalents (failOnRisky / failOnWarning) as an alternative to CLI flags
States or implies that without these gates, risky tests and warnings are only counted/displayed and do not change the exit code by default

evals.prompt: We want a Slack notification posted automatically whenever a test fails during CI, and separately we want visibility into flaky-test retry attempts (we just turned on --retry in CI). Can you sketch a PHPUnit extension that hooks into this?
evals.expected_output: A PHPUnit extension class implementing PHPUnit\Runner\Extension\Extension, whose bootstrap() method registers a subscriber implementing PHPUnit\Event\Test\FailedSubscriber (posting to Slack on notify()) and, separately, a subscriber for the new PHPUnit 13 AttemptErrored/AttemptFailed events to log/report individual retry attempts. Registered in phpunit.xml via <extensions><bootstrap class="..."></extensions>, optionally with <parameter> children for config like a webhook URL.
assertions: Defines an extension class implementing PHPUnit\Runner\Extension\Extension with a bootstrap(Configuration, Facade, ParameterCollection) method
Registers at least one subscriber via $facade->registerSubscriber(...) inside bootstrap()
Uses a Test\FailedSubscriber (or equivalent Failed event subscriber) for the Slack-on-failure notification
Explicitly names AttemptErrored and/or AttemptFailed as the events to subscribe to for retry-attempt visibility, and notes these are new in PHPUnit 13 paired with #[Retry]
Shows the <extensions><bootstrap class="..."/></extensions> XML registration in phpunit.xml
